case_title: JAGJIT SINGH v. STATE OF PUNJAB
statutory_provisions: IPC s.304-B, s.113-B of Evidence Act
aggravating_circumstances: Cruelty and harassment for dowry demand
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under s.304-B IPC, sentence reduced to 7 years
high_court_outcome: Affirmed conviction, reduced sentence to 7 years
neutral_facts: The accused, a man, was married to a woman who died along with her child by drowning in a river within seven years of their marriage. The prosecution alleged that the accused subjected the deceased to cruelty and harassment related to dowry demands. The deceased visited her sister's house and called her father, reporting harassment. The father and sister testified about the harassment, and a doctor opined that the death occurred around February 16-17, 2001. The trial court convicted the accused under s.304-B IPC, but the High Court reduced the sentence. The accused claimed there was no cruelty or dowry demand, but the courts found the evidence of harassment sufficient to invoke the presumption under s.113-B of the Evidence Act.
